headline: The bogus 1.16 in HRRR hour is gone; the new HRRR run instead has a real-looking but modest burst of 0.46 in in 3 hours from 1 to 4 AM Wednesday, at the 1:12 AM high tide, while the other models stay light and the rating card stays at none.

summary.text: The 11 AM HRRR drops the false 1.16 in hour but brings its own burst: 0.26 in at 1 AM Wednesday, 0.46 in for 1 to 4 AM. Earlier HRRR hours topped out at 0.16 in.
Wettest 3 hours: HRRR 0.46 in (GFS copies it), NBM 0.07, RRFS 0.02, ECMWF 0.02. HRRR is the wet outlier; NWS's 0.5 to 1 in Peninsula range sides closer to it.
Rating card consensus 0.07 in: no street flooding expected. HRRR alone (× 1.25) is 0.57 in, still under Yellow (garage) at about 0.71 in per 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour.
Dry through Tuesday afternoon. Light rain from late Tuesday evening; HRRR's heaviest 1 to 4 AM Wednesday, over by mid-morning. Thanksgiving dry; more rain likely this weekend.
HRRR's burst lands on the 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM Wednesday, running about 8.4 ft with surge, so the channel drains slowly then. Channel now low: 0.12 ft at noon.
Before Tuesday evening: clear street drain grates and yard drains. Overnight Tuesday: gusts to 35 to 45 mph can cut power to the pumps; move cars out of the cul-de-sac if it rains hard.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Dry and cool today; NWS San Francisco (12:40 PM) again calls today the day to clear drains and gutters. A cold front tied to an intense low off the Pacific Northwest crosses the Bay Area Tuesday night into Wednesday morning. NWS now says the moisture plume will run more south to north than earlier forecasts showed, putting the heaviest rain to our north and making this a less impactful system than first advertised. NWS rain totals: 0.5 to 1 in for the San Mateo Peninsula and Santa Cruz Mountains, 0.2 to 0.5 in for the interior Bay Area. Gusts 25 to 35 mph Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday morning, up to 45 mph near the Bays. Isolated thunderstorms are possible over the coastal waters and North Bay; abnormally warm coastal water could feed a strong cell with a localized heavy downpour. Thanksgiving and Friday dry; another storm likely this weekend into early next week. The Coastal Flood Warning for the Bay shoreline was reissued at 1:10 PM and runs to 4 PM Thursday.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
The false HRRR value flagged in the 8 AM correction (1.16 in at 1 AM Wednesday) is gone from the new 11 AM HRRR run. In its place HRRR now has a short burst at the same time, and this one looks physically plausible: it builds from 0.03 in at midnight to 0.26 in at 1 AM, then 0.09, 0.11 and 0.10 in through 4 AM. It is not a single isolated spike, but no other model supports that intensity, so treat it as HRRR's version of the front's rain band rather than a consensus.

Wettest 3 hours / storm total, 1 PM Monday to 1 PM Thursday:
• HRRR (11 AM Mon run, extended to 10 AM Wed): 0.46 / 0.58 in, wettest 1 to 4 AM Wednesday. Feed value 8 AM was 1.30 / 1.55 in with the bad hour.
• RRFS (4 AM Mon run): 0.02 / 0.04 in, wettest around 10 PM Tuesday to 1 AM Wednesday. Down from 0.08 / 0.16 in. NWS notes RRFS brings the front in slower and weaker.
• NBM: 0.07 / 0.14 in, steady 0.01 to 0.02 in per hour 11 PM Tuesday to 4 AM Wednesday. Little changed (0.04 / 0.12 in).
• ECMWF: 0.02 / 0.04 in, nearly dry. Little changed.
• GFS: identical to HRRR hour for hour, so it adds no independent information.
• HRRR 15-minute (ends 11:45 PM Tuesday): only 0.008 in per 15 minutes in the last hour before midnight, consistent with the hourly run.

Consensus (HRRR 0.46 × 1.25 = 0.57, RRFS 0.02, NBM 0.07): middle value 0.07 in, little changed from 0.08 in, so the rating card stays at none. The consensus is probably too low here: NWS's Peninsula total (0.5 to 1 in) matches HRRR far better than RRFS, NBM or ECMWF, and HRRR has under-forecast big local bursts here by about 3×. Even so, HRRR's hardest hour (0.26 in, 0.32 in with the bias) is below the 0.40 in one-hour Yellow trigger.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model runs about 1.3 to 1.4 ft above the predicted high tides at Redwood City and 0.9 to 1.2 ft above the lows. This morning's 9.2 ft high at 10:20 AM ran about 10.5 ft. Tonight's 7.0 ft high at 12:16 AM Tuesday runs about 8.4 ft; Tuesday's 9.5 ft high at 11:02 AM about 10.8 ft.

The timing matters this time: HRRR's burst (1 to 4 AM Wednesday) sits right on the 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM. The model has the water at 8.2 ft at 1 AM, about 8.4 ft near 2 AM, 7.8 ft at 3 AM and 6.5 ft at 4 AM, so the channel would drain slowly during the heaviest rain and better after about 4 AM. Rain earlier Tuesday evening falls near the -1.5 ft low at 6:28 PM (model about -0.4 ft), when draining is easy. Wednesday's 9.5 ft king tide at 11:46 AM comes after the rain ends; the model run stops at 7 AM Wednesday, so it gives no surge figure for that tide.

NWS (1:10 PM): Coastal Flood Warning for the San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines to 4 PM Thursday, with up to 2.7 ft of inundation possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. San Francisco highs 2.4 ft above normal Tuesday, 2.7 ft Wednesday and 2.2 ft Thursday, including up to 1.5 ft of surge, approaching the highest tide ever recorded there.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas it reads 0.12 ft at noon, flat between 0.12 and 0.15 ft for 24 hours (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at 5:13 AM, its latest report (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry on the street. The Caltrain rain gauge recorded no rain in the 24 hours to 5:13 AM, its latest report. NWS reports high clouds over the region with lingering low clouds inland clearing this afternoon.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Low through Tuesday afternoon: dry. Moderate to high for late Tuesday night into Wednesday morning. The split is wide: HRRR has a 0.46 in burst in 3 hours, the other independent models 0.02 to 0.07 in. NWS's own Peninsula totals favor the wetter side, and a strong cell on the front could briefly exceed any model. The worst case on current guidance is HRRR's burst verifying on the 1:12 AM high tide: sidewalk-level ponding is plausible, but street flooding to garage level would need about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour on the dashboard scale, more than even HRRR shows, or a downpour no model has.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Today and Tuesday morning: clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains; check sandbags.
• Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday morning: gusts 25 to 35 mph, up to 45 mph near the Bay; outages can slow the pumps.
• Tuesday night: if heavy rain is falling around midnight to 4 AM, move cars out of the cul-de-sac and take timestamped photos at the peak.
• Keep this page open overnight Tuesday; the next discussion will check whether HRRR holds its burst.
• Stay away from the Bay shore and tidal sloughs at the late-morning high tides through Thursday; don't walk or drive through moving water.
